children: The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment spurred by regional equity-market weakness. There are "concerns over elevated interest rates, persistent inflation pressures and the unwinding of crowded AI-related positions," UOB Global Economics & Markets Research says in a report. Based on technical analysis, however, the U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair's upward momentum has faded following its recent pullback, two members of the research team note. The U.S. dollar has probably entered a range-trading phase between S$1.2885 and S$1.2915, they add. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 1.2898 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
